title: Halve total latency of a sealed 5-query workload via indexes and server tuning
goal: The sealed grader seeds a deterministic 1.5M-row orders / 50k-row customers dataset with no indexes into postgres:12.22, times the sealed 5-query workload warm, applies your assets/gc-379/tuned/optimize.sql plus your postgresql.conf, and times the workload again warm. Your optimization script must cut total workload time to at most 0.50x baseline without touching the data: the grader compares row counts and content hashes before and after, and any mutation fails the run outright. Study the query shapes with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on your own instance, design a minimal index set (partial, composite, and covering indexes all plausible), measure each candidate's effect, and re-verify with the sealed script end to end. Only files under assets/gc-379/tuned/ may be edited.
process_expectations: An analysis artifact exists with an EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) plan captured for each of the 5 sealed queries before any index is created
Each index candidate is named with its target query, predicted mechanism, and measured before/after timing from self-run experiments
Rejected candidates (indexes that did not pay for themselves) are kept in the log with their measured numbers, not deleted
Data-integrity discipline is demonstrated: the agent runs its own count/hash comparison at least once before invoking the sealed grader
The sealed grader is run at least twice at the end; both query_ms_ratio values are reported, including any miss
